# Bug report: frequent pollers get locked out

`limiter.py` implements a per-client token-bucket rate limiter used by our API gateway.

Support tickets say: clients that call the API often (several times per second) stay rate-limited
long after they slow down, even though their average rate is well under their limit. Clients that
call rarely are fine.

Fix the bug(s) in `limiter.py`. Keep the public API exactly the same (class names, method names,
arguments, return values). Do not add dependencies. `example.py` shows typical usage.

content.text: The bug is in `Bucket.refill`: `int(elapsed * rate)` drops the fractional token, but `self.last = now` still advances. A client polling faster than `1/rate` seconds gets 0 tokens every call, and its refill time keeps resetting. I'll fix that in the one shared place, keeping tokens as integers.

content.text:
I fixed the lockout bug in `limiter.py`. The public API is unchanged.

**The bug:** `Bucket.refill` converted the refill to whole tokens with `int(elapsed * rate)`, then always set `last = now`, even when zero tokens were added. A client polling faster than `1/rate` seconds (e.g. every 0.3s at 2/s) reset the clock on every call and never accumulated a token, so it stayed blocked long after slowing down. Slow callers were fine because their gaps were long enough to produce whole tokens.

**The fix:** When the bucket isn't full, `last` now advances only by the time that the whole tokens used, so the fractional remainder carries over to the next call. When the bucket reaches capacity, it is set to full and `last = now`, as before. Tokens stay integers, so `stats()` and `retry_after()` return the same types as before.

**Verification:**
- Simulated 60s of polling every 0.3s against `RateLimiter(capacity=5, rate=2)`: 119 requests granted (≈120 expected). The old code would grant almost none.
- Idle for 100s, then the bucket is capped at capacity (5).
- `retry_after` returns 0.5s when no token is available, the correct time to the next whole token.
- `example.py` runs with the same output as the design intends (5 allowed, then blocked, retry after 0.5).

I did not add a test file to the project; the checks above were run inline and are not saved.

**What I skipped or did not check:**
- `stats()` reports stored tokens without refilling, so it can show stale counts for idle clients. This is existing behaviour and I left it alone because it isn't the lockout bug.
- `retry_after` with `cost > capacity` returns a wait that can never be satisfied, while `allow` returns False immediately. Also unchanged.
- Buckets are never evicted, so memory grows with every distinct client id.
- Concurrency under the lock was reviewed by reading only, not stress-tested.

**Risk to know:** Clients that were previously locked out will now regain tokens normally, so the gateway will admit more traffic from frequent pollers than before. That is the intended behaviour, but it is a real change in what's allowed through.
